rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.francesa.e1: Defence: let us think from Black's side, in the French Defence, Advance Variation. The black pawns on d5 and e6 stand on light squares.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.francesa.e2: The bishop on d7 also moves on the light squares, and its own pawns close its diagonals. A bishop shut in behind its own pawns is called a bad bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.francesa.l1: The bishop on f1 goes to e2 and prepares castling. It moves on the light squares, and the white pawns on c3, d4 and e5 stand on dark ones: its diagonals stay open. It is a good bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.francesa.l2: In positions like this, the side with the bad bishop tries to bring it outside the chain or to trade it for an enemy piece. The position decides the way.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.e1: Defence: again with Black, now in the Caro-Kann Defence, Advance Variation. The black pawns on c6 and d5 already stand on light squares.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.e2: If the pawn on e7 goes to e6 now, the bishop on c8 is shut in behind the chain, as in the French. For now, its diagonal to f5 is open.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.l1: The bishop comes out to f5 before the chain closes.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.l2: The knight on g1 goes to f3 and defends the pawn on d4, the base of the white chain.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.l3: Only now does the pawn go to e6: it opens the way for the bishop on f8, and the one on f5 is already outside.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.carokann.l4: In positions like this, the bishop that would become bad comes out before the chain closes. Outside it, the bishop has open diagonals and plays like a good bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.e1: Attack: now with White, in the Game Tabliiito × aBoris-1961, Lichess 2025. The white pawns on c3, d4, e5 and f4 stand on dark squares.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.e2: The bishop on g6 moves on the light squares with open diagonals: it is a good bishop. The black bishop on c8 is shut in behind the pawns on a6 and e6, in the light chain of b5 and d5.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.p: Find the move of the good bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.certo: The bishop captures the pawn on h7 with check and mate.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.revela: The bishop captures the pawn on h7 with check and mate. The knight on g5 defends the bishop and the f7 square, and the pawn on h6 takes g7 from the king.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.e1d1.1: The king captures the knight on d1, but the bishop on g6 is still attacked by the pawn on h7.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.e1d1.2: The pawn captures the bishop, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.e1d1.3: Back to the position: the good bishop still has an open diagonal to the king.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.g5h7.1: The knight captures the pawn on h7, but leaves g5, from where it covered h7 and f7, the mating squares.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.g5h7.2: The rook captures the pawn on f4, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.err.g5h7.3: Back to the position: the knight on g5 is already doing its job. Play with the bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.fora: That move does not use the bishop on g6. Play with it.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.volta: Try again: use the open diagonal of the good bishop.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.l0: On h7, the bishop gives mate: the open diagonal took it to the king.
rot.goodBadBishop.ideia.bom.l1: In positions like this, the good bishop attacks along the squares of its colour, and the opponent's bad bishop, shut in behind its pawns, cannot come to defend.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: White to move, in the Game Ustas1969 × Banyoe, Lichess 2017. The white pawns on a3, c5 and d4 stand on dark squares.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.2: The bishop on d3 moves on the light squares, and its diagonal to a6 is open. Behind it, the queen on e2 looks along the same diagonal.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.l.3: The bishop goes to a6 and gives check, supported by the queen on e2.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.l.4: The knight captures the bishop: it is Black's only move, because the rook on b1 takes b8 from the king.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.l.5: The queen captures the knight with mate.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra.l.6: In positions like this, the open diagonal of the good bishop reaches the enemy king. With the pawns on the other colour, it also opens the way for the queen.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: again with White, in the Game caluix × Deutsche_Reich, Lichess 2020. The black bishop on d7 moves on the light squares, like the pawns on b7, c6, d5, f7 and h7.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.2: It is a bad bishop. Look at the dark square g7, next to the black king: that bishop cannot defend it, and, besides the king, only the queen on f6 watches it.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.l.3: The queen enters g7, a dark square, and gives check, supported by the pawn on h6 and the rook on g1.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.l.4: The black queen captures the queen: it is the only move, because the king cannot capture it and has no free square.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.l.5: The pawn on h6 captures the queen with mate: from g7 it gives check, and the rook on g1 defends it.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.regra2.l.6: In positions like this, against a bad bishop, the pieces come in on the squares of the other colour. The bishop can never get there to defend.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: White to move, in the Game Lobino × benjaminvoges, Lichess 2019. The bishop on d3 moves on the light squares, like the white pawns on b5, c4, d5, f3, g4 and h3.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.2: By the colour of the pawns, it is a bad bishop. But the diagonal from d3 to g6 is open, and the black rook on e8 has only the king as a defender.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.l.3: The bishop goes to g6 and checks the king, the only defender of the rook on e8.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.l.4: The king captures the bishop. If it fled, White would win just the same: if it goes to f8 or g8, the rook captures the rook on e8 with mate.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.l.5: The rook captures the rook on e8, and White wins material.
rot.goodBadBishop.demos.excecao.l.6: In positions like this, a bad bishop comes out of the chain and is still worth a lot when it has an open diagonal outside. Before judging the bishop, look at the diagonals it uses.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.bom.err.f2f8: 29.Rf8+? gives check, but after 29...Nxf8 White loses the rook, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.bom.enunciado: Game Spekt_Rus × chessgod_ankit, Lichess 2022. You have two bishops: from the colour of your pawns, work out which is the good bishop and find the best move with it.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.bom.fim: The good bishop captured the queen on e6 with check and mate, along the open diagonal from h3 to e6.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.casas.err.f8f7: 36.Rxf7+? captures the pawn with check, but after 36...Kc6 the king escapes, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.casas.err.f8d8: 36.Rd8+? gives check, but after 36...Kc7 the king attacks the rook, and Black has a decisive advantage.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.casas.enunciad: Game lanalb × naucrates, Lichess 2018. Look at the colour of the black bishop on b5 and of the black pawns. Play as White and come in on the squares that bishop does not defend.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.casas.fim: The queen came in on the dark squares, d8 and d6, and gave mate with the support of the pawn on e5. The bad bishop on b5 defends none of them.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.casas.vez1.err: 37.Qc8+? gives check, but after 37...Kb6 the king escapes to b6, and the position is equal.
37.Qe8+? gives check, but after 37...Kb6 the king escapes, and the position is equal.
37.Rxf7? captures the pawn, but after 37...Qc1+ Black gives mate in two moves.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.valeAqui.err.f: 40.Qe6+? gives check, but after 40...Kg7 the king leaves the diagonal, and the position is equal.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.valeAqui.err.c: 40.c6? advances the pawn, but after 40...Rc5 the rook stops it, and the position is equal.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.valeAqui.enunc: Game melksham × mma0105, Lichess 2024. By the colour of your pawns, is the bishop on d3 good or bad? Before deciding, look at its diagonals. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.goodBadBishop.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The bishop came out of the chain to c4 and gave mate along the diagonal to g8. By the colour of the pawns it would be a bad bishop, but here the diagonal outside decides.
